01

Identity and context

Musqueam is a contemporary community with enduring relationships to the lower Fraser River and Vancouver region.

Read the sources [1] Musqueam / UBC Museum of Anthropology teaching resource

02

A path for deeper reading

Focus the next stage of research on: Community naming, hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ language, land and self-government. The sources below are selected reading paths; their authorship, dates and community scope should guide how they are used.

Read the sources [1] Musqueam / UBC Museum of Anthropology teaching resource [2] www2.gov.bc.ca [3] www2.moa.ubc.ca

03

Continuity within a changing estuary

Musqueam’s own account locates community life near the Fraser River mouth and emphasizes continuity despite assimilation policies. The teaching timeline connects colonial politics with community experience. These accounts should be read as Musqueam interpretation, alongside the original records where specific legal or historical claims need examination.

Read the sources [4] Musqueam Indian Band [1] Musqueam / UBC Museum of Anthropology teaching resource

04

Language documentation and learning

The Language & Culture department describes long-term documentation, its orthographic choices and a learning partnership with UBC. Its explanation supplies a route into community-directed study. Neither undated speaker statements nor language decline establish that the community has disappeared.

Read the sources [5] Musqueam Language & Culture department

05

A dated view of a specifically connected place

Metro Vancouver’s 2022 background paper records collaboration with Musqueam over Iona Island ecological priorities and project design. The 2006 Iona Beach photograph introduces that named setting before the described project. It does not show completed restoration, grant visitor rights or settle land ownership.

Read the sources [6] Metro Vancouver

Historic Timeline — selected Musqueam teaching resource ↗

A Musqueam-voiced teaching timeline places colonial policies and community persistence together. It is an interpretive educational work, not the original legislation or court record.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual timeline introduction and selected Fraser Delta, trade, colonial policy, Indian Act and organizing entries:reader lines5–9, 23–25, 41–58, 75–91. Sensitive burial/remains descriptions and creation narratives are not reproduced.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Normal HTTP200 HTML/text read. Displayed headings and dates do not always align in text extraction; no legal chronology is inferred from heading positions. Original laws, testimony, cases, linked chapters and videos uninspected.

https://www2.moa.ubc.ca/musqueamteachingkit/history.php

Musqueam’s Story — selected continuity and place introduction ↗

Musqueam presents itself as a continuing community whose history and livelihood are connected with lands and waters near the Fraser estuary.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual opening community/Fraser-mouth paragraph, name introduction and concluding continuity paragraphs. Public narratives were encountered but are not reproduced.

Language — selected history, orthography and learning partnership ↗

The department explains decades of documentation, its writing-system choices and educational collaboration with UBC. Programme aims are distinct from measured proficiency.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual history/orthography explanations, partnership paragraph beginning Since 1997, and departmental objectives. Pronunciation text was encountered; no audio was played.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Normal HTTP200 body read. Linked lessons, recordings, charts and course outcomes uninspected. Undated fluency claims and present schedules are not adopted; language loss does not establish people’s disappearance.

Iona Island conceptual-design background paper — selected Musqueam engagement account, 2022 ↗

Publication: 2022-05

This agency account documents specific Musqueam collaboration and ecological priorities at Iona Island. Supporting place context for the dated landscape, not another broad Musqueam history.

Inspection: Supporting or limited review; see scope

Scope: Actual complete PDF/printed p.9, Reconciliation and First Nations Engagement; cover date May 2022. The34-page file was obtained but not fully read.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Normal HTTP200 PDF/text read. Statements are 2022 agency-reported priorities and plans, not confirmed completion, unanimous consent, or a present title/access determination. Renderings and project maps not reused.
